result.description: Work management platform for teams to organize tasks, projects, portfolios and goals.
result.auth_detail: OAuth2 auth-code (+PKCE, 1h access token + refresh) for multi-user apps; personal access token (bearer) for own/internal use; Service Account token (Enterprise only); OpenID Connect for sign-in.
result.access_detail: Create PAT or OAuth app in developer console self-serve; OAuth apps usable by any Asana user. Docs state no plan restriction for the API; service accounts need Enterprise; Enterprise admins can control apps/PATs. View-only license users have limited API access. Plan-level free-tier limits not explicitly confirmed on fetched pages.
result.api_notes: REST at app.asana.com/api/1.0, JSON. Covers tasks, projects, portfolios, custom fields, webhooks, users, teams, app components, plus audit log and SCIM on Enterprise. Rate limits apply per token.

evidence.quote: A personal access token (PAT) is the quickest and simplest way to authenticate in the API.
This is the best choice if multiple users need to sign in to your app.
You can generate a personal access token from the Asana developer console.
View only license users have limited access to the API.
The Asana API is a RESTful interface with predictable resource-oriented URLs
Asana's official MCP server lets you interact with your Asana workspace through natural language
The Asana V2 MCP server is generally available and uses OAuth for authorization.
